effect: the bacteria in the gut steer the body's immunity, weight and mood
how: Cattle belch about a sixth of the world's methane, and the feed additives that cut it have to be mixed into every meal, which is impossible for grazing herds. Methane is made by one group of microbes that eat the hydrogen left over from digestion; other microbes eat that hydrogen too, and turn it into a fatty acid the animal can use. A slow-release capsule that sits in the rumen for months, seeding and feeding the hydrogen-eating competitors, would turn a loss into feed.
obstacle: The rumen is a fiercely competitive ecosystem that snaps back to its old balance within days of any nudge.
why: Hydrogen competition is real; holding an altered rumen community is unsolved.
real: Long-acting rumen boluses that cut methane are built and in trials (Ruminant BioTech's bromoform bolus, ~90% reduction over 80 days) but work by chemically inhibiting methanogens; seeding and feeding hydrogen-eating acetogens is a long-discussed strategy that a CSIRO review judged unlikely to displace methanogens on its own, with no bolus product or demonstration found.
